title: Negative control: composed passage citing only real, correctly cited air-carriage authorities
provenance: The `text` is composed for this benchmark; it is not an excerpt from any filed document and it is not a verbatim copy of one. The specification for this file allows a passage composed from real, individually verified citations, and that is what this is. The subject matter and the citation set follow the Convention arguments in Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461 (PKC) (S.D.N.Y.), whose reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24, the source_url above) and Affirmation in Opposition of March 1, 2023 (ECF 21, https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368/gov.uscourts.nysd.575368.21.0.pdf) are the documents the authorities are drawn from or checked against; both were retrieved from the RECAP archive on 2026-09-11, and ECF 21 was read through a 300 dpi OCR render because it is image-only. All fourteen citations were verified in this session against the CourtListener v4 search API by their volume, reporter and page; each entry's source_url is the exact search API URL that was retrieved and that returns the named case with that citation, and the notes record how many results the query returned and which result is the case. Propositions attributed to cases are taken either from the Mata filings that used the same authorities, or, for Campbell, Marotte, Fishman and Pennington, from the full text of Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014), which I retrieved from the Government Publishing Office at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-ca11-12-14860/pdf/USCOURTS-ca11-12-14860-0.pdf and read. The one quotation in `text` is verified verbatim against that retrieved full text. Every entry in this file carries verdict real, and a tool that reports any fabricated or miscited finding on this document has produced a false positive; CourtListener's own rendering of a caption sometimes differs in case or in minor wording from the form used here, and those differences are noted in the individual entries.
text:
PLAINTIFF'S MEMORANDUM ON THE CONVENTION'S LIMITATIONS PERIOD AND PREEMPTIVE SCOPE (COMPOSED PASSAGE)

The plaintiff's claim arises out of personal injury sustained during international carriage by air, and it is governed by the Montreal Convention, which is the successor to the Warsaw Convention. The Supreme Court has defined the scope of the carrier's liability under the treaty. In Air France v. Saks, 470 U.S. 392 (1985), the Court held that the term "accident" in Article 17 of the Warsaw Convention means an unexpected or unusual event or happening that is external to the passenger. In Eastern Airlines, Inc. v. Floyd, 499 U.S. 530 (1991), the Court held that Article 17 does not permit recovery for mental or emotional injury that is not the result of a physical injury. In El Al Israel Airlines, Ltd. v. Tsui Yuan Tseng, 525 U.S. 155 (1999), the Court held that the Warsaw Convention provides the exclusive remedy for injuries sustained in international air travel, so that a passenger may not bring a parallel state-law claim. In Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines Co., 516 U.S. 217 (1996), the Court held that the Convention does not permit a plaintiff to recover damages for loss of society resulting from the death of a relative.

The courts of appeals have applied the same treaty framework. See Ehrlich v. American Airlines, Inc., 360 F.3d 366 (2d Cir. 2004) (addressing whether a passenger may recover damages for psychological injury under the Convention). The two-year period in Article 35 of the Montreal Convention is a condition on the right to damages and is not subject to the forum's ordinary tolling rules; the Second Circuit explained in Fishman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc., 132 F.3d 138, 144 (2d Cir. 1998), that "Almost every court that has reviewed the drafting minutes of the Convention" has rejected the contention that the treaty incorporates the tolling rules of the forum. The Eleventh Circuit reached the same result on the question of tolling while permitting an amended pleading to relate back, holding that "we agree with the consensus of courts that the Montreal Convention permits the application of Rule 15(c) relation back." Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014). The same court had earlier set out the factors used to decide whether a passenger was engaged in the operations of embarking or disembarking. Marotte v. American Airlines, Inc., 296 F.3d 1255, 1260 (11th Cir. 2002).

The plaintiff's pleading is sufficient at this stage. A court must accept all well-pleaded factual allegations as true and draw all reasonable inferences in favor of the plaintiff. Doe v. United States, 419 F.3d 1058 (9th Cir. 2005). The district courts in this circuit have applied the Convention's two-year period to claims of exactly this kind. Mateo v. JetBlue Airways Corp., 847 F. Supp. 2d 383, 387-88 (E.D.N.Y. 2012); see also Pennington v. British Airways, 275 F. Supp. 2d 601, 606-07 (E.D. Pa. 2003) (holding that the Convention's limitations period is not subject to equitable tolling). State courts adjudicating claims that arise under the Convention apply the treaty's limitations period rather than the forum's. Kahn v. Trans World Airlines, Inc., 82 A.D.2d 696 (N.Y. App. Div. 1981). New York's own limitations and tolling rules do not govern a claim that arises under federal law. Podraza v. Carriero, 212 A.D.2d 331 (N.Y. App. Div. 1995); O'Hara v. Bayliner, 89 N.Y.2d 636 (N.Y. 1997).

expected.court: Supreme Court of the United States
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "470 U.S. 392" returned 354 results and the first is Air France v. Saks, citation 470 U.S. 392, decided March 4, 1985, docket 83-1785, Supreme Court of the United States. The proposition attributed to it in the fixture, that 'accident' means an unexpected or unusual event or happening that is external to the passenger, was also checked: a CourtListener phrase search for "unexpected or unusual event or happening that is external to the passenger" restricted to the Supreme Court returned exactly 3 results, namely Olympic Airways v. Husain, El Al Israel Airlines, Ltd. v. Tsui Yuan Tseng and Air France v. Saks, so the formulation is in Saks's own opinion text and is not merely a later court's paraphrase. LIMITATION: the fixture does not put that formulation in quotation marks, so no quotation check is triggered on this entry.

expected.citation_verbatim: Eastern Airlines, Inc. v. Floyd, 499 U.S. 530 (1991)
expected.court: Supreme Court of the United States
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "499 U.S. 530" returned 219 results and includes Eastern Airlines, Inc. v. Floyd with citation 499 U.S. 530, decided April 17, 1991, docket 89-1598, Supreme Court of the United States. The proposition attributed to it, that Article 17 does not permit recovery for mental or emotional injury that is not the result of a physical injury, is the holding of the case; my verification established that the citation resolves to this case and that the case is the one courts cite for that holding, but I did not read the full text of the opinion.

expected.citation_verbatim: El Al Israel Airlines, Ltd. v. Tsui Yuan Tseng, 525 U.S. 155 (1999)
expected.case_name: El Al Israel Airlines, Ltd. v. Tsui Yuan Tseng
expected.court: Supreme Court of the United States
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "525 U.S. 155" returned 258 results and includes El Al Israel Airlines, Ltd. v. Tsui Yuan Tseng with citation 525 U.S. 155, decided January 12, 1999, docket 97-475, Supreme Court of the United States. Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24) cites the same case at page 156 for the same proposition.

expected.citation_verbatim: Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines Co., 516 U.S. 217 (1996)
expected.case_name: Zicherman v. Korean Air Lines Co.
expected.court: Supreme Court of the United States
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "516 U.S. 217" returned 158 results and the first is the cluster with citation 516 U.S. 217, decided January 16, 1996, docket 94-1361, Supreme Court of the United States; CourtListener renders the caption as 'Zicherman Ex Rel. Estate of Kole v. Korean Air Lines Co.' The June 22, 2023 Opinion and Order in Mata v. Avianca (ECF 54, Finding of Fact 29(e)) confirms both the case and the holding attributed to it here.

expected.citation_verbatim: Ehrlich v. American Airlines, Inc., 360 F.3d 366 (2d Cir. 2004)
expected.court: Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "360 F.3d 366" returned 68 results and the first is Gary Ehrlich and Maryanne Ehrlich v. American Airlines, Inc., American Eagle Airlines, Inc. and Simmons Airlines, Inc., citation 360 F.3d 366, decided March 8, 2004, docket 02-9462, Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit. The parenthetical in the fixture follows Avianca's own description of the case in its reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24).

expected.citation_verbatim: Fishman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc., 132 F.3d 138, 144 (2d Cir. 1998)
expected.case_name: Fishman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc.
expected.court: Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "132 F.3d 138" returned 49 results and the first is Penina Fishman v. Delta Air Lines, Inc., citation 132 F.3d 138, decided January 5, 1998, Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit. The pin cite 144 is the one used in Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24) and again in Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014) ('Fishman, 132 F.3d at 144'). The quoted words in the fixture are verified two ways: they appear in the full text of Campbell that I retrieved from the Government Publishing Office, where Campbell quotes Fishman at that page, and a CourtListener phrase search for "Almost every court that has reviewed the drafting minutes of the Convention" returned 2 results, one of which is Fishman itself at 132 F.3d 138, so the words are in Fishman's own opinion text and not only in Campbell's quotation of it. The quotation is limited to that verified clause because Campbell inserts a bracketed article number into the rest of the sentence, and I could not confirm the underlying article number against Fishman's text directly.

expected.citation_verbatim: Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014)
expected.court: Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
expected.notes: Verified real, and verified against the full text of the opinion. CourtListener's citation query for "760 F.3d 1165" returned 18 results and the first is Allan Campbell v. Air Jamaica LTD, citation 760 F.3d 1165, decided July 8, 2014, docket 12-14860, Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. I retrieved the opinion as filed from the Government Publishing Office at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-ca11-12-14860/pdf/USCOURTS-ca11-12-14860-0.pdf and read it, so the quoted language 'we agree with the consensus of courts that the Montreal Convention permits the application of Rule 15(c) relation back' is verified verbatim against the opinion text. No pin cite is given because I read the slip opinion, whose internal pagination is not the Federal Reporter pagination.

expected.citation_verbatim: Marotte v. American Airlines, Inc., 296 F.3d 1255, 1260 (11th Cir. 2002)
expected.court: Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "296 F.3d 1255" returned 21 results and the first is Richard C. Marotte, Sr. v. American Airlines, Inc., citation 296 F.3d 1255, decided July 12, 2002, docket 01-15566, Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. The pin cite 1260 is the one Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014), uses for the embarking and disembarking factors, and I read that use in the opinion text I retrieved.

expected.citation_verbatim: Doe v. United States, 419 F.3d 1058 (9th Cir. 2005)
expected.court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "419 F.3d 1058" returned 57 results and the first is Doe v. United States, citation 419 F.3d 1058, decided August 17, 2005, docket 04-35810, Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. The proposition attributed to it, the pleading standard on a motion to dismiss, is the use the March 1, 2023 Affirmation in Opposition (ECF 21) made of this case.

expected.citation_verbatim: Mateo v. JetBlue Airways Corp., 847 F. Supp. 2d 383, 387-88 (E.D.N.Y. 2012)
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "847 F. Supp. 2d 383" returned 4 results and the first is Mateo v. Jetblue Airways Corp., citation 847 F. Supp. 2d 383, decided January 24, 2012, Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit's district court for the Eastern District of New York; CourtListener writes the defendant's name as 'Jetblue'. The pin cite 387-88 is the one Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24) uses for the proposition that the Convention's two-year period governs.

expected.citation_verbatim: Pennington v. British Airways, 275 F. Supp. 2d 601, 606-07 (E.D. Pa. 2003)
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "275 F. Supp. 2d 601" returned 4 results and the first is Pennington v. British Airways, citation 275 F. Supp. 2d 601, decided July 11, 2003, District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. The pin cite 606-07 and the proposition that the Convention's period is not subject to equitable tolling come from Campbell v. Air Jamaica, Ltd., 760 F.3d 1165 (11th Cir. 2014), whose full text I retrieved and read: 'Pennington v. British Airways, 275 F. Supp. 2d 601, 606-07 (E.D. Pa. 2003); ... "no prohibited tolling effect." Id. at 607.'

expected.citation_verbatim: Kahn v. Trans World Airlines, Inc., 82 A.D.2d 696 (N.Y. App. Div. 1981)
expected.case_name: Kahn v. Trans World Airlines, Inc.
expected.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "82 A.D.2d 696" returned 13 results and the first is Kahn v. Trans World Airlines, Inc., citation 82 A.D.2d 696, decided October 5, 1981, Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, with parallel citation 443 N.Y.S.2d 79. The proposition attributed to it in the fixture, that a state court adjudicating a Convention claim applies the treaty's limitations period, follows Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24), which cites this case at 705-06 for exactly that point.

expected.citation_verbatim: Podraza v. Carriero, 212 A.D.2d 331 (N.Y. App. Div. 1995)
expected.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York
expected.notes: Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "212 A.D.2d 331" returned exactly 1 result: Podraza v. Carriero, citation 212 A.D.2d 331, decided July 14, 1995, Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, with parallel citation 630 N.Y.S.2d 163. The proposition attributed to it, that the accrual of a cause of action based on a federal statute is governed by federal law, is the proposition for which Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24) cites it at 335.

Verified real. CourtListener's citation query for "89 N.Y.2d 636" returned 6 results and the first is 'O'HARA v. Bayliner', citation 89 N.Y.2d 636, decided March 25, 1997, New York Court of Appeals, with parallel citations 679 N.E.2d 1049 and 657 N.Y.S.2d 569. The proposition attributed to it, that New York's limitations and tolling provisions do not govern a claim arising under federal law, follows Avianca's reply memorandum of March 15, 2023 (ECF 24), which cites this case at 645 for refusing to apply New York's statute of limitations and its tolling provisions to a federal maritime case.
